resolved.title: Hello World
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Hello World[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Let's kick things off by creating a simple program that displays the text "Hello world!".

In Python, we use the [b]print [/b]function to output text.

So to generate our message, the code would look like this:
[code format="py" codeId="3884"][b]print[/b]('Hello world!')[/code]
Nice work! You’ve just written your first Python program. Easy, right? You’ll be triggering the singularity in no time!
[note]The [b]print [/b]statement is always followed by parentheses containing the output we want to generate.[/note]

resolved.title: 打印多行文本
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Printing Text[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

More to say? Of course you do!

You can use the [b]print [/b]statement to output multiple lines of text.

[s0l0!-header][b]For Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="py" codeId="3886"]print('Hello world!')
print('Hello world!')
print('Spam and eggs...')[/code]
Each [b]print [/b]statement will output its text on a new line.
[note]Python code contains lots of references to [b]Monty Python[/b]. So you’ll see "spam" and "eggs" used as placeholder variables.[/note]
